answer: Behavioral trace clustering flags sybils after the fact. The system builds a graph of shared transaction timing across an atlas of agent interactions; dense clusters entering through one inlet get re-scored against verified history. Accounts whose traces correlate above threshold are quarantined from a shared lagoon of reputation, forcing attackers to maintain distinct timing patterns per identity. Each masked identity costs the attacker continuous independent scheduling and delayed payouts, roughly doubling operational overhead per fake account.
